description: The webview may invoke this app's own named commands and nothing else: llm_complete, llm_status, web_search, load_state, save_state, keep_unreadable_state, ocr_image, ocr_status, engine_status, engine_wake, engine_warm, engine_sleep, engine_set_idle_unload, models_status, models_download, models_download_picture, models_download_embedding, models_download_projector, models_cancel, models_on_this_mac, models_remove, chat_complete, personas_list, task_complete, tasks_list, screen_capture, screen_capture_status, pigeon_take_opens, pigeon_run, pigeon_check_ride, pigeon_use_new_revision, play_permission, play_ask, play_open_settings, play_windows, play_preview, play_key_test, play_start, play_stop, play_status, play_hud, pigeon_save_drawing, pigeon_example_drawings, pigeon_contents, pigeon_inspect_pick, set_dev_menu, pigeon_add, pigeon_remove, patch_status, open_main_window, popover_hide, popover_show, bar_hide, bar_show, bar_fit, bar_bubbles, main_hide, app_restart, save_chat, remove_chat, settings_peek, window_theme, log_event, diagnostics_log, logs_save, logs_reveal, diagnostics_copy — sixty-seven of them. save_chat takes a chat's id (letters, digits, dashes, underscores — one file name, never a path) and its JSON and writes app_data_dir/chats/<id>.json; remove_chat takes an id; settings_peek takes nothing and returns the theme, the last wake time, and the game last played with the way each game takes keys, from state.json, so the menu-bar windows never read every chat for one line. main_hide takes nothing and does what ⌘W does: the main window goes to the menu bar; app_restart takes nothing and restarts this app, for a Patch update. window_theme takes one of dark, light or system and sets only the main window's own appearance to match, so its title bar is drawn in the colours the page chose; it returns nothing. No shell, no filesystem plugin, no network of its own — core:default is the entire granted surface. tauri-plugin-dialog is registered in lib.rs for pigeon_inspect_pick's and pigeon_save_drawing's own use, but none of its commands are added to invoke_handler, so this stays true: the webview cannot open a picker itself, it can only ask Rust to import a Pigeon. Note that app-registered commands are NOT gated by this file; capabilities govern plugin permissions. The boundary is enforced by what invoke_handler registers in lib.rs and by what each command accepts: a role, a query, a JSON string, image bytes, or nothing — never a URL, a host or a path. pigeon_inspect_pick is the one exception in form only: it takes nothing and returns what it found — names, kinds, statuses and ids — but the path it resolves comes from a native OS picker, never from the page. pigeon_save_drawing takes an installed Pigeon's id and the recipe text it answered with — never markup and never a path — draws that recipe again in Rust from the Pigeon's own parts table, and writes only that SVG to a place the person picks in a native save dialog, returning the file's name alone. pigeon_example_drawings takes an installed Pigeon's id and returns its card's example recipes drawn in Rust from its own parts table, as markup in memory, writing nothing. pigeon_contents takes an installed Pigeon's id and returns its material's section titles, read here and with no model involved, so a "that isn't in here" reply can name what is. pigeon_inspect_pick and pigeon_add split an import in two so a file can be DESCRIBED before it is on the Mac: the first picks and reports, installing nothing, and the second installs only the ids the person ticked — ids this shell handed out, which expire, and which name bytes already held in memory here rather than any path. pigeon_run may also carry one picture for a Pigeon whose base sees, as a data:image URL Rust checks is one — never a path or a URL to fetch — which goes only to the picture server Rust starts on its own loopback port. pigeon_check_ride and pigeon_use_new_revision take an installed Pigeon's id: the first asks it the examples its own kept file carries and, if it misses any, puts back the version it replaced; the second is the person choosing the new one anyway. What either retires is moved to the Trash, never deleted. The play_ commands let a picture Pigeon play a window: they take an installed Pigeon's id, a window id the watcher itself listed, a way to send keys (one of three words) and a watch-only switch — never a path, a key or a URL. Keys pressed come only from that Pigeon's actions.json, never with a modifier, never while another app is in front, and a global ⌘⇧. registered only while it plays stops it; the Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions are asked in Pigeon's own process when the person presses the button. pigeon_remove takes an installed persona's id — the name personas_list already gave the page — and refuses anything that is not one plain file-name component, so it cannot be turned into a path; the adapter, sidecar, payloads and kept original it deletes are all built in Rust inside app_data_dir. patch_status returns what Patch is — name, version, sealing key, prompts, tunables, categories and the base his code is served from — as data, never a path; a skill pack imported through pigeon_add is checked as Patch and stored in app_data_dir/patch for the next launch, and patch-changed is emitted when one is. load_state/save_state touch exactly one file, app_data_dir/state.json, whose path is built in Rust; keep_unreadable_state takes nothing and moves that same file aside when this build cannot parse it, to a sibling name chosen here, so an unreadable history is kept rather than overwritten by the next save. engine_set_idle_unload takes a number of seconds and accepts only the three periods Settings offers, so a page cannot ask for weights to be held all day. set_dev_menu takes on or off and rebuilds the menu bar with or without the Developer menu; what is in that menu is decided in appmenu.rs, never sent by the page. ocr_image hands the bytes to the Mac's own Vision recogniser through the bundled pigeon-eye (or to a Tesseract a person has named) and never writes them to disk. engine_warm takes nothing and asks nothing: it loads Patch's base, his router, asks check and planner, and a lane's context ahead of the question the typing promises, so the turn after an idle unload does not pay for them. engine_wake spawns the bundled llama-server (or adopts one already on its port) with std::process::Command on a path resolved in Rust, never through a shell plugin; models_download fetches the two files pinned by URL and SHA-256 in models.json into app_data_dir/models and nowhere else. models_download_picture takes nothing and does the same for the picture model models.json pins beside them — its base, and its projector into models/projectors — and only when a person asks for it from Peek. models_download_embedding takes nothing and fetches the one embedding model models.json pins — the search model a Pigeon that answers from its own material needs to embed a question — into that same folder, only when a person asks for it from such a Pigeon's page; the material's own vectors arrived inside the .pigeon, so the model is never asked to read a document. models_download_projector takes a projector's sha256 and nothing else: Rust looks that hash up in the sealed base registry this build ships with, fetches the projector from the address, size and hash the registry gives into models/projectors, and keeps it only when its SHA-256 matches — the page never supplies the URL, the host or the file name, and a hash the registry does not list is refused. A picture Pigeon that leaves out its stock projector asks for it from the Meet sheet, which shows its size, source and licence first. models_on_this_mac lists that same folder — every model this Mac keeps, since Flight School borrows Pigeon's rather than keeping its own — and models_remove takes an entry that list produced, never a path: anything else is refused, one another app relies on waits for the page to confirm, and removal is a move to the Trash. chat_complete is the one command through which a model may write words a person reads: it speaks to the chat endpoint, never the router's, and names every adapter with its scale so nothing it sends can change what the router is asked. Asked with peek, it writes on the picture server instead (Peek: the picture model with every picture Pigeon on it turned off), and only then may it carry one picture, as a data:image URL Rust checks is one — never a path or a URL to fetch. task_complete is a THIRD door and narrower than either of the others: the page names a TASK from a closed set in task.rs and supplies only text, never the instruction, so it cannot become a second way to make a model write arbitrary prose. It wears a task adapter, turns the category adapter and every persona off, and runs greedy at temperature 0 with a fixed seed, because a repair must come back the same way twice. What it returns is INPUT: the page audits it and shows it beside the original for the person to choose between. core:event is what lets a page listen to the events those commands emit, and to pigeon-meet, fired when a .pigeon opened via Finder is checked while the window is already up. screen_capture takes no path and hands back a PNG made in memory; the picture never touches disk, and the macOS screen-recording prompt is raised from inside that command and nowhere else. TWO windows are named here, not one. The popover is the menu bar's, and it is granted the same core:default as the main window because it runs the same pipeline and needs the same three things: core:event to hear the engine's status, core:window to hide itself when it loses focus, and core:webview for its own page. It is a smaller surface, not a weaker one — a value it answers carries the same provenance the window would give it, and it reaches the same named commands and no others. What it does NOT get is anything the main window does not already have: this line widens the boundary by one window label and by nothing else. core:window's default set holds only getters, so the popover cannot hide or show itself either: popover_hide and popover_show take nothing and act on that one window, which is what Escape and stepping out of its own screenshot use. A THIRD window is named too: the summon bar, which ⌘⇧P brings up from anywhere (bar.rs). It is granted the same core:default for the same reasons and runs Patch and only Patch — it never reaches the chat lane. core:default gives no window a way to hide, move or size itself, and the bar is not given one: bar_hide and bar_show take nothing, bar_fit takes a height in points that bar.rs clamps, and bar_bubbles takes open or shut and how many bubbles are drawn, which bar.rs holds to three or four, so where the bar is, how wide it is and how tall it may get are decided in Rust. The key chord itself is registered from Rust through tauri-plugin-global-shortcut, none of whose permissions appear below, so no page can register, change or listen for a shortcut. A FOURTH window is named: the play overlay (playhud.rs), a small panel that shows what a playing Pigeon sees and the key it last pressed, with Stop and Hide. It is granted the same core:default so it can hear play-event, and it reaches play_status, play_stop, play_hud and open_main_window and nothing it would need a model for. Rust brings it up when a play starts and places it; play_hud takes only true or false, so where it sits and how big it is are not the page's. It is never made key, so the game underneath keeps the keyboard. ONE custom URI scheme is registered in lib.rs, pigeon-pack, and it is not a command and not a capability: it is read-only, answers GET only, and serves only the active sealed pack's code/**/*.js bytes from memory — never a prompt, the seal, the adapter or any file on disk — to these three windows and no other label, under the prefix patch_status names. It exists so the skills worker can import Patch's code; the page CSP (script-src 'self' pigeon-pack:, worker-src blob:, connect-src without any outside host) leaves that worker unable to eval, build a function from a string, or fetch any other origin, which was measured in an embedded WKWebView build rather than assumed. log_event takes a kind word and a JSON object of fields and returns nothing; Rust cuts every text in it to 80 characters except the plan, drops pictures and anything under ~/.airoplane-mode, and appends one line to the day's file in app_data_dir/logs, whose path the page never learns. diagnostics_log takes nothing and returns text: the build, Patch, the engine stamp, the macOS version, the model files by name and size, memory now, and the log lines of the last 60 minutes; the page puts that with the open chat on the clipboard and sends it nowhere. logs_save takes a range word (today, 7, 30 or custom) and, for custom, two dates — never a path — joins those days of app_data_dir/logs under the same header as diagnostics_log, and writes that one text file where the person picks in a native save dialog, returning its name alone; saving is the only way the log leaves the Mac. logs_reveal takes nothing and opens app_data_dir/logs in Finder. diagnostics_copy takes the text the page built from diagnostics_log and the open chat, at most 8 MB, and puts it on the Mac's general pasteboard from Rust, because WebKit refuses a page's own clipboard write once the click has waited on anything; it returns the number of characters and sends nothing anywhere. Adding a capability here without a matching named command is how the boundary gets lost.
